description.value: Clinical and neuroimaging features of frontotemporal dementia due to C9ORF72 mutations, including comparisons of C9ORF72 expansion carriers and sporadic noncarriers using voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: Here, we describe clinical and neuroimaging features seen in symptomatic C9FTD/ALS carriers at the Memory and Aging Center at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF).

description.value: An observational comparison of symptomatic C9ORF72 expansion carriers, sporadic noncarriers, and healthy older adult controls.

spans.text: The present findings suggest that C9ORF72 mutation carriers are likely to receive a clinical diagnosis of FTD, ALS, or FTD-MND.
Group differences were compared using glm, χ2, or Fisher exact test depending on data type.

Clinical and neuroimaging data were compared between C9+ (15 behavioral variant FTD [bvFTD], 11 FTD-motor neuron disease [MND], 5 amyotrophic lateral sclerosis [ALS]) and sporadic noncarriers (48 bvFTD, 19 FTD-MND, 6 ALS).

spans.text: Here, we describe clinical and neuroimaging features seen in symptomatic C9FTD/ALS carriers at the Memory and Aging Center at the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF).
All C9+ patients displayed clinical syndromes of bvFTD, ALS, or FTD-MND.
The most common diagnosis among C9+ carriers was bvFTD (48.4%), followed by FTD-MND (35.5%) and ALS without dementia (16.1%, table e-1).
Comparison patients met criteria for bvFTD (international bvFTD research criteria [FTDC]15; n = 48), ALS (clinically definite or probable El Escorial Criteria16; n = 6), or FTD-MND (n = 19).

clinical_characteristics.value: Patients had more delusions and greater working-memory impairment, but milder eating dysregulation than bvFTD noncarriers; MRI was acquired within 1 year of the first UCSF visit.
